author: A. Stein
evidence: Stein cleared a Kushan Buddhist stūpa near the Ṭabar-kōt mound at the entrance of the Thal plain, with an undisturbed relic deposit, Graeco-Buddhist carvings and Kharoṣṭhī and Brāhmī sherds: "the first Buddhist ruin discovered in Baluchistan". He also surveyed the Duki–Sanjawi mounds of Loralai.
quote: the first Buddhist ruin discovered in Baluchistan, belongs to the Kushāna period
note: No Xuanzang link. Buddhism in Loralai is attested, but for the Kushan period; Xuanzang reports 伐剌拏 monasteries mostly in ruins.

asr_identification: Sehwan (Lambrick's candidate for 臂多勢羅; alternative only)
evidence: Sehwan, identified with Alexander's Sindimana and the Arab geographers' Sadūsān, was the capital in Arab times of a province reaching to the borders of Makran (Chachnāma); its mound holds only a Muhammadan-period fort.
quote: The province of which it was the capital in the Arab times comprised
note: No Xuanzang link; bears on Lambrick's Sehwan for 臂多勢羅, which the surface remains do not support for the 7th century.
